The information you've heard is not accurate for the transition generation (birth years 1961–1969). Women born between 1961 and 1969, when they reach the age of 64, continue to receive the regular AHV (Alterste Invaliden Versicherung) pension. However, it's important to note that the AHV pension is not the only source of income for this group during their retirement years. Many women in this cohort also benefit from additional sources of income, such as their own contributions to occupational pension schemes, private savings, or the earnings of a spouse or partner. 

There is no special benefit or compensation for women born in this period that is tied to early retirement. The AHV pension serves as the foundational income, and its amount is calculated based on the individual's average earnings throughout their working life, among other factors. If a woman in this age group decides to retire early, she may receive a reduced pension, but this reduction is not specific to her gender or birth year. It applies to all individuals who choose to retire before the full retirement age.
